chunks: Safwan narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who spends on another man who is not among his dependents, except that he takes it upon himself to provide his maintenance and clothing. Is his zakat al-fitrah upon him? He said: “No. His fitrah is only upon his dependents as charity, not upon that one.” And he said: “Dependents are the child, the owned servant, the wife, and the umm al-walad.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a bondwoman who bore a child for her master
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: the owned servant or slave under one’s care
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child counted among one’s dependents
key_terms.صَدَقَةً: charitable due, here referring to the obligatory fitrah payment
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: his dependents or household members for whom maintenance is recognized
key_terms.فِطْرَتُهُ: the zakat al-fitrah due on behalf of a person
key_terms.نَفَقَتَهُ: his financial maintenance or living expenses

ai.seo_question: Is zakat al-fitrah obligatory for someone whom a person supports voluntarily but who is not part of his household?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on zakat al-fitrah, stating that it is only due on those who are counted among a person’s dependents. Voluntarily supporting someone financially does not by itself make their fitrah obligatory upon the supporter. The Imam عليه السلام also identifies key categories of dependents, including children, slaves, wives, and umm al-walad.
